“Work No. 36.” This piece is displayed standing upright inside a case made of tempered glass. The display, adorned with metal decorations and stained glass, is a perfect fit for a work that was once used as a model.

[3_01_artwork.jpg]

*Text on the white plaque*

・Work No. 36
・Created on May 12 (birthday).
・Created by her father and mother.
・Real name: Kirara Sera
・Measurements: Height 167, Bust 112, Waist 66, Hips 100
・Weight: 58 kg
・Although she once worked as a model and possessed a voluptuous figure, she refused even swimsuit photo shoots, stating, “I absolutely do not want to do any risqué work.” Due to her excessive selfishness, she was dropped by her agency and donated to this museum.

Her greatest appeal is, without a doubt, her voluptuous figure. Her breasts, which look as if they’re about to burst, boast an astonishing size of 112. With her curvaceous figure—from her buttocks to her thighs—she would surely have been worshipped as a goddess in a different era.

Despite all this, she strongly dislikes being looked at with “ulterior motives.” Even when she was working as a model, she refused any work that was even slightly risqué—she wouldn’t even do swimsuit photo shoots. This must have been quite a challenge for her agency, which wanted to promote her based on her physique.

However, this exhibit has been designed with her in mind. This glass case becomes transparent when an electric current is applied; normally, it appears frosted.

[3_02_artwork.jpg]

However, this glass turns transparent whenever the subject becomes aroused. Whether it’s sexual arousal, of course, or excitement from feeling anger, laughing from being tickled, or even the thrill of drowning during water torture—the glass turns transparent.

If, by any chance, she were to reach orgasm, the glass would become completely transparent. If the subject doesn’t want her body to be seen, she must remain calm at all times. I wonder if a spoiled “princess” could actually manage that.

[3_03_artwork.jpg]

Back when she was still a human, she worked as a model while attending school. Although she was blessed with stunning looks, her personality was terrible. She was always late for work and reportedly complained a lot. She was particularly harsh toward women and seemed to have a especially bad attitude toward staff and male fans.

Her agency signed her because of her voluptuous figure, but the jobs that came her way were all of a suggestive nature. Not wanting to be looked at with lecherous eyes, she reportedly turned down many of them.

This was because she had once won a junior beauty pageant. Because of that, she probably believed, “I’m being appreciated for my cute face.” Of course, there’s no doubt she was a stunning beauty, but it seems most people were only looking at her body.

Her voluptuous body is truly worthy of being called a work of art. If you bring your face close enough to examine it carefully, her short temper might cause her to lose her cool instantly, and you might even catch a glimpse of what lies beyond the frosted glass. Please be sure to admire this artistic physique in its entirety.
